Measure m92 at 10/1, 50 uL, EA loading; predicted V1/V2 approximately 8.35/29.19 mL. The new matched-load 20/1 observation 66da447ca0fe7160cc1c is 13.96/34.55, whereas the 150-uL curve decreases from 29.54 to 21.38 mL in completion between 10/1 and 20/1 (ad0ace61c29817c678c2, e9dc948c0e68a88eb621). This determines whether the reversal is confined to the higher loading.

Measure m92 at 20/1, 100 uL, EA loading; predicted 9.43/28.23 mL. This completes the loading triplet between measured 50-uL 13.96/34.55 and 150-uL 5.42/21.38 (66da447ca0fe7160cc1c, e9dc948c0e68a88eb621). The model currently interpolates; the failed m127 middle-load prediction shows why that interpolation needs measurement. Together with the selected 10/1 low-load row, this distinguishes loading dependence from solvent-response shape.

Measure m194 at 2/1, 100 uL; predicted 5.04/21.43 mL. Measured completion is 14.73 at 50 uL (2bd4f8787a951ef0ee04) and 28.18 at 150 uL (2bb48a2862bf80c30a36), with much less onset variation. The middle point tests the newly learned loading dependence and whether the large completion difference is smooth, without imposing the failed m127 interpolation assumption.

Measure meta-amino ester m88 at 1/1, 100 uL; predicted 6.12/15.29 mL. At identical loading, 2/1 gives 11.89/21.50 (ca6feb29f6758377a65f) and the new 5/1 label gives 27.58/64.40 (85924bdd0693438dc23a), whose completion was underpredicted by 22.80 mL at acquisition. This locates the strong-eluent end of the steep response and tests whether the repair is confined to 5/1.

Measure tertiary-amino acrylate m19 in pure EA at 150 uL; predicted 8.44/11.76 mL. Its 100-uL labels at 1/1 and 2/1 are 12.36/25.23 and 16.43/32.81 (9a60cb4735780275034e, 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07), both previously underestimated. This tests the predicted collapse in completion under stronger eluent in a different amine environment. Loading differs from those anchors, so the result will constrain a joint condition response rather than an isolated solvent effect.

Measure dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate m91 at 2/1, 50 uL; predicted 7.57/4.94 mL, an invalid endpoint ordering. Pairing it with the selected 1/1 row at identical loading tests whether the model has misplaced onset, completion, or both across this strong-eluent segment. Measured 5/1 at 100 uL is a valid 7.29/11.12 (a2ecf2b2f28094d70368).

Measure m91 at 1/1, 50 uL; predicted 6.80/4.39 mL. This second inversion forms a controlled solvent pair with the selected 2/1 row. Measuring both constrains the extent of the failure across conditions, rather than supplying only one corrected interval for the model to interpolate around.

Measure dodecyl acrylate m18 in pure EA at 150 uL; predicted 5.93/4.92 mL, with both endpoint and completion-quantile ordering problems. The prior 1/1 inversion was replaced by a measured 5.85/7.42 interval at 50 uL (5265c3d2f02abb35e86e). This tests whether the remaining pure-EA failure represents an incorrectly learned strong-eluent limit; the different load prevents treating it as a pure solvent contrast.

Measure dimethoxybenzaldehyde m125 at 2/1, 100 uL, DCM 300 uL; predicted 32.97/69.61 mL. Exact loading matches measured 1/1 at 7.50/20.47 (4c32851430464f0ed684) and 5/1 at 42.96/73.10 (74cf50c6ec476a394b01). The existing 2/1 label uses 150 uL and DCM 500 uL (facbcedbecb46072b04c). This tests the sharp predicted transition with those loading confounds removed.

Measure dibenzylamine m212 at 5/1, 100 uL; predicted 7.17/13.68 mL. The measured 5/1, 50-uL interval is 7.24/13.67 (d5234e966aa231be05e5), while 10/1 at 100 uL is 46.67/78.07 (70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73). Matching the latter loading tests whether this unusually sharp solvent transition survives removal of the load difference and prevents generalizing the m19 or amino-ester response to every amine.

Measure acetophenone oxime m11 at 1/1, 100 uL; predicted 3.61/17.42 mL. Matched measured 2/1 and 5/1 intervals are 4.70/12.12 and 6.93/15.70 (c3c4fdce502f6d3576dc, 1182373ab8814dbe2f43). Thus the model predicts a strong-eluent completion maximum. High CW distance supports investigating this gap, but the paired observed curve is the main reason for selection.

Measure salicylaldehyde m197 at 2/1, 100 uL; predicted 4.90/16.22 mL. Matched pure-EA and 1/1 observations finish at 26.73 and 25.53 mL (ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3, 69be7348f9ab10739164). This tests a substantial predicted completion decrease in weaker eluent in a molecule whose strong-eluent intervals are already measured. Related substituted salicylaldehyde predictions have failed, so their behavior should not be transferred without this local check.

Measure bromosalicylaldehyde m190 at 10/1, 100 uL; predicted 10.17/31.05 mL. Its matched 2/1 and 20/1 labels are 5.94/16.82 and 7.57/29.88 (b73454f4c6942f4deb70, d1774335b45258bc173a). It fills a missing segment and pairs with pending positional isomer m186 at 10/1. The isomer comparison retains density and loading-volume differences as covariates; it tests transfer of response shape rather than attributing differences solely to substitution position.

Measure ortho-methoxyacetophenone m127 at 20/1, 100 uL; predicted 5.72/31.41 mL. The new 50/1, 100-uL label is 35.44/35.52 (a3ae677aae8a8faf5786), radically unlike the two other 50/1 loads. The measured 20/1, 150-uL anchor is 5.08/31.97 (ebdeaba52880c7a7b0f). This determines whether the anomalous middle-load onset is restricted to 50/1 or extends to the adjacent solvent segment.

Measure benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester m78 at 5/1, 100 uL; predicted 8.09/18.75 mL. Matched 20/1 and 50/1 observations are 22.20/43.60 and 49.93/97.97 (a44a22945d76c02aa6a7, 61771d230b285babe4b6). This fills the stronger-eluent segment of a rising carbonyl response and contrasts with the shallow measured aromatic beta-ketoester m81 curve (db2709229820b71e283b, 57646b9484b03f4076bb). It tests structural transfer beyond carbonyl count.

Measure amino enoate m72 in pure EA at 100 uL, loaded in DCM 200 uL; predicted 4.53/18.91 mL. The measured pure-EA row a047be17b8ee8bebb29a has the same density and sample volume but PE 300-uL loading, yielding 4.46/19.50. The predictor expects little change. This directly tests sensitivity to the recorded loading protocol in a polar nitrogen-containing compound; solvent identity and loading-solvent volume change together, so their individual effects cannot be separated.

hypotheses.content: The previous smooth-interpolation hypothesis for m127 at 50/1 is rejected: its middle loading does not interpolate either endpoint. Whether the unusual 100-uL onset is confined to 50/1 remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The 35.44/35.52 middle-load label can distort neighboring predictions if interpreted as a smooth loading law. A neighboring solvent condition tests the locality of that record without assigning an unobserved mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 20/1 and 100 uL, does onset remain near the measured 150-uL onset of 5.08 mL, or also become unusually late?

hypotheses.content: Loading-associated endpoint differences in m92 and m194 are substantial, but their intermediate responses and interaction with solvent ratio remain unresolved. They should be learned locally rather than through a universal monotonic loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: m92 completion decreases with greater loading at 20/1, whereas m194 completion increases with loading at 2/1. Measuring connected conditions can constrain molecule-condition interactions and discourage inappropriate transfer of either trend.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m92 show the same solvent reversal at 50 uL as at 150 uL, and do the m92 and m194 middle loads interpolate their respective measured endpoints?

hypotheses.content: Current endpoint inversions identify local prediction failures, but correcting one condition does not ensure valid or accurate neighboring intervals. Both endpoints need measured constraints across the affected segment.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m62 repair required lowering both endpoints, whereas the m18 repair lowered onset and raised completion. The m91 pair and m18 pure-EA extension test whether similar failures recur in common low-volume ester regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What measured intervals replace the m91 strong-eluent crossings and the remaining m18 pure-EA crossing, and which endpoint contributes most to each failure?

hypotheses.content: Nonmonotonic recorded solvent responses are molecule- and endpoint-specific. Some apparent reversals disappear under matched loading, some persist, and predicted extrema should be tested against local observations rather than accepted or rejected as a class.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: m115 retains a matched-loading completion decrease from 5/1 to 10/1, while the m194 low-load comparison and m129 result remove previously suspected maxima. These different outcomes argue for local response constraints and against a global reversal correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted m11 strong-eluent maximum and m197 2/1 decrease measured features, and does the m190 10/1 segment resemble the pending m186 positional isomer?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing compounds have distinct solvent-response transitions that are not adequately summarized by the presence of an amine or nitrogen acceptor alone. Recent m88 and m19 labels expose underpredicted completion, while m212 may have a much sharper transition between 5/1 and 10/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Missing strong-eluent segments and a matched-loading m212 comparison test whether the model can distinguish aromatic amino esters, a tertiary amino acrylate, and a secondary benzylamine. Silica acid-base and hydrogen-bond interactions are plausible priors, not established explanations for the recorded differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How rapidly do m88 and m19 completion volumes fall under stronger eluent, and does m212 retain its short 5/1 interval when loading matches the much longer 10/1 observation?

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels reject smooth interpolation for m127: the 100-uL 50/1 result is 35.44/35.52 mL, rather than an onset between 1.01 and 11.65 with completion near 23.7. I therefore test the neighboring solvent segment, not another assumed loading law. m194 at 2/1 and 50 uL finishes at 14.73, below its matched 5/1 completion of 21.52; its earlier apparent reversal was loading-confounded. In contrast, m115 at matched 100-uL loading finishes at 30.66 at 5/1 versus 20.15 at 10/1, preserving that recorded reversal. m92 at 20/1 and 50 uL gives 13.96/34.55, substantially above the 150-uL label, motivating a small connected loading/solvent experiment. m129's 5/1 result rejects its predicted completion maximum. The m117 pure-EA and 1/1 measurements give completion of 13.48 and 20.23 at identical loading, opposite to the previously predicted pure-EA elevation. The m62 and m18 inversion tests produced valid intervals but required different endpoint corrections. m21's 50/1 rise was predicted well, so I do not immediately repeat that extension. m166 and m81 were comparatively accurate at their new weak-eluent segments, reducing their follow-up priority. The m88 and m19 completion underpredictions motivate missing strong-eluent measurements. Recent CW results additionally expose m141 and m122 onset underprediction, but pending experiments already provide related nitrogen and methoxy-aromatic coverage. All error statements refer to acquisition-time predictions, not current residuals.
batch_rationale: The pending batch supplies broad coverage of aromatic, ester, boronate, and nitrogen-containing rows. This supplement adds comparisons that geometric coverage alone does not resolve: m92 has a connected solvent/loading design, m194 tests a newly revealed completion-loading relationship, and m127 tests the boundary of an irregular record. The matched m91 pair and m18 extension constrain failures in small-volume intervals, while m11, m197, and m190 test specific response-shape questions. m88, m19, m212, m125, and m78 locate transitions in chemically connected families; m72 tests a recorded loading-protocol contrast that the predictor currently treats as nearly invariant. These labels may improve generalization by teaching where solvent strength, structure, and loading interact, while avoiding excessive replication of recently accurate segments. No selection is intended to maximize retention or improve separation performance. Quantile widths are single-predictor outputs with visible ordering defects, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is an elution interval. Unrecorded experimental variation remains a possible contributor to irregular labels. The supplement contains 16 distinct supplied candidate IDs, avoids pending IDs and duplicate experimental tuples within the supplement, and uses only the supplied observed records as measured evidence.
